front_blocks.md: Define **zwitterion**.

back_blocks.md: A **zwitterion** is a species that carries both a positive (-NH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup>) and a negative (-COO<sup>-</sup>) charge on the same molecule. Amino acids form zwitterions in aqueous solution.

front_blocks.md: Why are amino acids described as amphoteric?

back_blocks.md: Amino acids contain both a basic **amino group** (-NH<sub>2</sub>) and an acidic **carboxylic acid group** (-COOH). They can act as both acids and bases, which is the definition of amphoteric.

cards.front_md: Why are amino acids described as amphoteric?

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
At low pH, the carboxylate group (-COO<sup>-</sup>) of a zwitterion accepts a proton to reform -COOH.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Adding acid lowers the pH. The -COO<sup>-</sup> group accepts an H<sup>+</sup> to reform the -COOH group, causing the zwitterion to become a **positively charged ion**.

front_blocks.md: Define **isoelectric point**.

back_blocks.md: An **isoelectric point** is the pH at which an amino acid exists predominantly as a neutral zwitterion, with no net overall charge.

cards.front_md: Define **isoelectric point**.

front_blocks.md: What happens to the -NH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup> group of a zwitterion when a base is added?

back_blocks.md: The -NH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup> group **donates** a proton (H<sup>+</sup>) to the added base, reforming the -NH<sub>2</sub> group. This causes the zwitterion to become a **negatively charged ion**.

front_blocks.md: The general structural formula for naturally occurring amino acids is **..........**. There are **..........**  naturally occurring amino acids.

back_blocks.md: The general structural formula for naturally occurring amino acids is **RCH(NH**<sub>**2**</sub>**)COOH**. There are **20** naturally occurring amino acids.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Amino acids are soluble crystalline solids because of the strong intermolecular forces between zwitterions.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Zwitterions carry both positive and negative charges, creating strong electrostatic attractions between molecules. This results in amino acids being **soluble crystalline solids**.

front_blocks.md: How does an amino acid solution act as a buffer?

back_blocks.md: The zwitterion can **accept protons** (via -COO<sup>-</sup>) when acid is added or **donate protons** (via -NH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup>) when base is added. This resists changes in pH, making it a buffer solution.

front_blocks.md: Define **peptide bond**.

back_blocks.md: A **peptide bond** is an amide bond formed between the -NH<sub>2</sub> group of one amino acid and the -COOH group of another in a condensation reaction, with H<sub>2</sub>O eliminated.

cards.front_md: Define **peptide bond**.
cards.back_md: A **peptide bond** is an amide bond formed between the -NH<sub>2</sub> group of one amino acid and the -COOH group of another in a condensation reaction, with H<sub>2</sub>O eliminated.

front_blocks.md: What small molecule is eliminated when two amino acids join to form a dipeptide?

back_blocks.md: **Water (H**<sub>**2**</sub>**O)** is eliminated. The -NH<sub>2</sub> group of one amino acid reacts with the -COOH group of another in a condensation reaction.

cards.front_md: What small molecule is eliminated when two amino acids join to form a dipeptide?
cards.back_md: **Water (H**<sub>**2**</sub>**O)** is eliminated. The -NH<sub>2</sub> group of one amino acid reacts with the -COOH group of another in a condensation reaction.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A dipeptide still contains free -NH<sub>2</sub> and -COOH groups that can undergo further condensation reactions.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
The dipeptide retains an -NH<sub>2</sub> at one end and a -COOH at the other. These can react with additional amino acids to form a tripeptide or polypeptide.

front_blocks.md: What is a polypeptide?

back_blocks.md: A **polypeptide** is a long chain formed when many amino acid molecules are joined together by peptide bonds through repeated condensation reactions.

back_blocks.md: A peptide bond is also called an **amide** bond. It is formed in a **condensation** reaction between the -NH<sub>2</sub> and -COOH groups of two amino acids.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A tripeptide is formed when three amino acids join, with two peptide bonds and two water molecules eliminated.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Each condensation step eliminates one water molecule and forms one peptide bond. Three amino acids joined in sequence produce two peptide bonds and release two H<sub>2</sub>O molecules.

cards.back_md:

front_blocks.md: Which two functional groups on an amino acid take part in forming peptide bonds?

back_blocks.md: The **-NH**<sub>**2**</sub>** (amino) group** and the **-COOH (carboxylic acid) group**. The -NH<sub>2</sub> of one amino acid reacts with the -COOH of another to form the peptide bond.

back_blocks.md: A **dipeptide** is a molecule formed when two amino acids are joined by a single peptide bond in a condensation reaction, eliminating one molecule of water.

front_blocks.md: Define **electrophoresis**.

back_blocks.md: **Electrophoresis** is an analytical technique that separates ions by placing them in an electric field. It is used in biochemistry to identify and purify proteins and amino acids.

cards.front_md: Define **electrophoresis**.
cards.back_md: **Electrophoresis** is an analytical technique that separates ions by placing them in an electric field. It is used in biochemistry to identify and purify proteins and amino acids.

front_blocks.md: In electrophoresis, what determines the rate at which an ion moves toward an electrode?

back_blocks.md: Two factors determine the rate:

1. **Size** of the ion: larger ions move more slowly.
2. **Charge** of the ion: more highly charged ions move more quickly.

cards.front_md: In electrophoresis, what determines the rate at which an ion moves toward an electrode?
cards.back_md:
Two factors determine the rate:

1. **Size** of the ion: larger ions move more slowly.
2. **Charge** of the ion: more highly charged ions move more quickly.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
In electrophoresis, positively charged amino acid ions move toward the positive electrode.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Positively charged ions move toward the **negative** electrode. Negatively charged ions move toward the positive electrode.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

In electrophoresis, positively charged amino acid ions move toward the positive electrode.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Positively charged ions move toward the **negative** electrode. Negatively charged ions move toward the positive electrode.

front_blocks.md: At pH 7, in what direction does lysine (a positively charged amino acid) move during electrophoresis?

back_blocks.md: Lysine moves toward the **negative electrode**. Its positively charged side chain means it is attracted to the negatively charged electrode.

cards.front_md: At pH 7, in what direction does lysine (a positively charged amino acid) move during electrophoresis?
cards.back_md: Lysine moves toward the **negative electrode**. Its positively charged side chain means it is attracted to the negatively charged electrode.

front_blocks.md: An amino acid at its isoelectric point will **..........**  during electrophoresis. Larger ions travel **..........**  slowly than smaller ions toward the electrode.

back_blocks.md: An amino acid at its isoelectric point will **remain stationary (in the well)** during electrophoresis. Larger ions travel **more** slowly than smaller ions toward the electrode.

cards.front_md: An amino acid at its isoelectric point will **..........**  during electrophoresis. Larger ions travel **..........**  slowly than smaller ions toward the electrode.
cards.back_md: An amino acid at its isoelectric point will **remain stationary (in the well)** during electrophoresis. Larger ions travel **more** slowly than smaller ions toward the electrode.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The charge on an amino acid during electrophoresis depends on the pH of the solution.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
The pH determines whether the amino acid is positively charged, negatively charged or neutral (at its isoelectric point), which in turn determines the direction and rate of migration.

front_blocks.md: What is an electropherogram?

back_blocks.md: An **electropherogram** is the series of bands observed on the paper or gel after electrophoresis. Each band corresponds to a particular species, separated by charge and size.
